parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes a Warm Homes Plan investing £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes, alongside mandating financial institutions to develop transition plans aligned with the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C goal. Labour also commits to reversing the Conservative decision preventing the Bank of England from considering climate change in its mandates.

citations.quote: Labour will invest an extra £6.6 billion over the next parliament, doubling the existing planned government investment, to upgrade five million homes to cut bills for families.

mandating UK-regulated financial institutions ­ including banks, asset managers, pension funds, and insurers ­ and FTSE 100 companies to develop and implement credible transition plans that align with the 1.5°C goal of the Paris Agreement.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives commit to reaching net zero by 2050 via a pragmatic and proportionate approach, emphasising private sector innovation, cost reduction for households, and scaling up nuclear power including Small Modular Reactors. They reject what they describe as Labour's top-down approach.

citations.quote: We will cut the cost of tackling climate change for households and business, and deliver net zero by 2050.
We reject Labour's dogmatic, top-down approach that will burden households with higher bills.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats commit to achieving net zero by 2045 at the latest, proposing an emergency Home Energy Upgrade programme, a rooftop solar revolution, and supporting British industry through measures including a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and investment in low-carbon industrial processes.

citations.quote: Liberal Democrats are committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2045 at the latest.
Implementing the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism for high-emission products, protecting UK businesses from unfair competition.
